findings: The black diagram panels in the 'A pluck is a chord' and 'Every room keeps a private list' sections are near-empty rectangles with a single thin horizontal line — they read closer to placeholder voids than resolved figures, the weakest craft moment on the page.
Some utility/caption text (the mono metadata strips under headings) is set so small and low-contrast it becomes near-illegible decorative texture rather than legible information.
The lower 'Sounding Log' index tables lean on fairly conventional ledger-row formatting; competent but the least distinctive zone.
what_works: Genuine editorial hero: high-contrast serif with a deliberately italicized 'still.' set left-aligned against a dark organic Chladni-plate render on the right — an asymmetric composition with real tension, not a centered tagline.
Consistent typographic voice — a contrasty book serif for display/body against a spaced uppercase mono for labels and catalog numbers — a committed pairing no default generator reaches for.

The whole page is structured as a physical catalog/log of vibrating plates (numbered figure rows, a '118 Sympathy' log entry with an oversized numeral, epoch notes), a specific conceptual conceit rather than a feature grid.
Restrained palette: warm paper ground, ink black, and a single oxidized rust-red used sparingly to mark one active table row and section rules.
A.reasoning: This is a deliberate editorial/catalog artifact — asymmetric serif hero over a textured plate image, a committed serif-plus-mono type system, and a paper/ink/rust palette used with restraint — none of which resembles the centered-hero-plus-gradient-plus-three-cards SaaS template. It clears the bar on hero and composition with a real signature. It falls short of the top band because a few of the black 'diagram' panels read as empty placeholder space and some mono metadata is illegibly small, softening the otherwise strong hierarchy.

what_works: Hero typography establishes immediate editorial voice with large serif display against restrained body text
Consistent left-margin vertical rhythm and red accent rules create a clear reading spine without centering or symmetry defaults
Interactive string and figure elements are integrated as native content rather than decorative overlays
B.reasoning: Desktop render shows a deliberate, text-first editorial composition with modular type hierarchy, restrained red accents on a near-monochrome field, and asymmetric layouts that avoid all listed slop states. No gradients, cards, or SaaS shapes appear; the hero is a strong typographic statement rather than a generic centered tagline. Minor deductions only for occasional dense text blocks that could tighten vertical rhythm further.
